note: Run 3 (2026-10-15): the keys are built from `solved` through the plate family's mesh (`npm run plates`); the declarations below are run 2's. Every key borrows its curve class, weight kind and lead from a named reference card of v3/references/owner/picks.json (`cards`, recorded with `eagle_board.py apply`; the card gives the class and kind, the bow, sign, lean and `over` are authored here) and names the plate family it is cut from (`plateFamily`: keys share a family only when one inbetweens to the other without a limb crossing the torso or the figure turning). `solved` is `solvePose` of the declaration (`npm run solve-poses`). Derived from the chart's eight keys and their prose (lineOfAction strings -> class/bow/sign, pose strings -> weight/lead/silhouette); bows, offsets and drifts are a first reading to be corrected on the plates, not measurements. heightPx is the rest figure's 922 px mask height: the keys' joints are the solved joints and the plates are the home mesh posed to them (D85, `npm run plates`), so the key space is the home mask space at scale 1. Bows are fractions of heightPx; the root-to-head chord is about a third of the height, so 0.06 is already a sagitta of 18 percent of the chord. Breakdowns are authored to the timing shape (TIMING_SHAPE in src/library/animation/pose.ts), not searched: every move is 3-6 drawings, one drawing per 4 frames from the end of the key's hold (the hold probe reads a longer run as a hold); passing drawings rise through 0.25-0.75 and are placed so the steps ease in and out (0.25 then 0.65 on a 3-drawing move); a settle at 0.95 lands on the chord (offset 0); awe -> brace opens with one anticipation (the left wrist drawn back before the brace). The arc offset sits on the root where the body travels (it carries head and arms) and on the lead wrist where it does not; its side follows the lead wrist's own bow and its size comes from the chord (0.2 of the root chord, at least what clears the arc reach on the least aligned joint; 0.15 of the wrist chord). One overshoot, on brace -> joy-a, where the chart's prose bursts ("the burst after the pop"): 1.15 along the chord (the top of the band) with half the passing arc, then the settle. Secondaries lag 2 drawings on twos (4 frames), one drawing of this shot's fours, so a trailing part changes on the body's own frames instead of between them. Each hand names its side: it does not lag on the moves its side leads, so the lead wrist is authored motion and the arc probe reads it as such. The brace moving hold drifts over its whole 24-frame hold (the probe measured 0.35 stage px over 16).

covers.why: the cloak's sleeves cover both hands until the lift (sp-1.1 'cloak covers both hands', sp-1.2 'hands visible after, not before'): the parts rig draws the hand parts from the lift's frame

keys.name: rest-on-lid
keys.moment: Upright behind the box, weight even, forearms resting on the lid's near edge, chin down, eyes on the lid.

twinned.why: the poster pose: even weight and both forearms resting the same way on the lid is the point of the first frame

keys.name: grip
keys.moment: Shoulders drop and round, elbows bend, fingertips curl under the lid's near edge: the gather before the lift.

twinned.why: both hands take the lid's near edge together: the gather is a matched grip, and the asymmetry starts on the lift, where the right arm leads

keys.name: lift
keys.moment: Arms rise to chest height pulling the lid, torso straightens and leans a little back, chin lifts.

keys.name: awe
keys.moment: One step back, arms drop open and low, palms out, head tipped back to follow the rising bubble.

keys.name: brace
keys.moment: Hands drawn in to the chest, shoulders up, weight leaning back on the heels, eyes fixed on the swelling bubble.

twinned.why: both hands are drawn in to the chest at once: the held breath is a closed, matched guard, and the asymmetry is the weight on the left foot and the left hand leading

keys.name: joy-a
keys.moment: Arms flung up and out, back arched, hips pushed to the left, face up: the burst after the pop.

keys.name: joy-b
keys.moment: The same joy turned the other way: hips to the right, arms swapped, the hair swoop swinging across (the turn).

keys.name: joy-c
keys.moment: The spin comes round: arms flung up and out again, hips back to the left, face up. Joy-a's drawing on purpose, the second half of one full turn.

keys.name: flinch
keys.moment: Hands drawn in to the chest, shoulders up, weight back on the heels: the first flinch as the pieces stop waiting their turn. Brace's drawing on purpose.

twinned.why: both hands are drawn in to the chest at once: the held breath is a closed, matched guard, and the asymmetry is the weight on the left foot and the left hand leading

keys.name: shrink
keys.moment: Knees bent, back rounded, chin to chest, forearms crossed over the head: small and covering, joy overrun by the field.

twinned.why: the figure folds in on itself with forearms crossed over the head; a symmetric closed shape is what covering looks like

keys.name: fold
keys.moment: The pieces keep coming and she goes lower: knees bent, hips sunk, back rounded over them, chin to chest, forearms crossed over the head. The shrink's drawing, folded down to the floor: the shortest she is in the beat.

twinned.why: the figure folds down on itself with the forearms crossed over the head: a symmetric closed shape is what covering looks like
